title: Master the Z-Score: Building Mean-Reverting MQL5 Trading Systems

for: Strategy 1: Classic Mean Reversion defines a precise entry condition: 'Z-Score crosses below -2.0 and then re-enters above -2.0' for buys, and symmetrically for sells — a discrete, binary, time-series event detectable in historical tick/bar data.
Strategy 1 exit rule is explicitly testable: 'Exit when Z-Score crosses back to 0.0', i.e., a threshold-crossing condition on the same computed Z-Score series.

The Z-Score formula is fully specified: (close[i] - mean) / std_dev, where mean = sum(close[i-j]) / InpPeriod and std_dev = sqrt(sum_sq_diff / InpPeriod), using population variance — enabling exact replication on historical OHLC data.
Input parameters are concrete and fixed per test: InpZPeriod = 20, InpUpperThresh = 2.0, InpLowerThresh = -2.0 — all directly pluggable into backtesting engines.

Three distinct, parameterized strategies (with explicit thresholds: ±2.0, ±2.5, ±1.5, and exits at 0.0 or ±1.0) are each accompanied by full MQL5 code implementing bar-by-bar logic — meaning every condition (crosses, comparisons, state transitions) is objectively verifiable on historical price series.

non_fatal: No spread or commission modelling in tests
No robustness analysis across market regimes (e.g., no regime filter validation beyond EMA trend filter in Strategy 3)
No discussion of parameter sensitivity or walk-forward stability

No justification for using population variance (N) vs sample variance (N−1) beyond 'computational efficiency' — though this is not a fatal flaw per se, it's a statistical choice with distributional implications

judge.formula_and_logic: Z-Score is computed as (current_close - SMA_N) / std_dev_N, where SMA_N is the N-period simple moving average of closing prices, and std_dev_N is the population standard deviation (using divisor N, not N−1) over the same N periods. Entry_long triggers on a discrete cross: Z-Score was < InpLowerThresh on the prior closed bar and ≥ InpLowerThresh on the current closed bar. Entry_short triggers symmetrically: Z-Score was > InpUpperThresh on the prior closed bar and ≤ InpUpperThresh on the current closed bar. Exit_long occurs when Z-Score ≥ 0.0; exit_short when Z-Score ≤ 0.0. All calculations use only fully closed bars — no look-ahead or future data.
judge.entry_long: Z-Score was < InpLowerThresh on previous closed bar AND Z-Score ≥ InpLowerThresh on current closed bar
judge.entry_short: Z-Score was > InpUpperThresh on previous closed bar AND Z-Score ≤ InpUpperThresh on current closed bar
judge.exit_rule: For long: Z-Score ≥ 0.0; for short: Z-Score ≤ 0.0

repaint.note: Z-Score is calculated exclusively on closed bars using rolling historical windows; no recalculation on incomplete bars or future data.

higher_tf.note: No higher time frame data is used; all calculations are on the current chart's timeframe.

tick_volume.note: Tick volume array is declared but unused in Z-Score calculation; only close[] is used.

source_quotes.quote: To compute the Z-Score for a financial instrument at any given price bar, we execute three distinct mathematical operations across a rolling window of length N: 1. Calculate the Simple Moving Average of the closing price over N periods: 2. Calculate the population variance across those same N periods: Note: While sample variance with Bessel's correction ($N-1$) provides an unbiased estimator... population variance ($N$) is intentionally utilized here... 3. Subtract the moving average from the current closing price and divide by the standard deviation:
Buy Setup: Z-Score crosses below -2.0 and then re-enters above -2.0. Exit when Z-Score crosses back to 0.0 (the mean).
Sell Setup: Z-Score crosses above +2.0 and then re-enters below +2.0. Exit when Z-Score returns to 0.0.

source_quotes.about: MQL5 implementation confirms use of two closed bars for cross detection
source_quotes.quote: Copies 2 readings from the indicator buffer starting at bar index 1 (the last fully closed candle)... Stores the Z-Score value of the most recently closed candle. Stores the Z-Score value of the candle right before that.
Exit when Z-Score crosses back to 0.0 (the mean).

judge.summary: Статья описывает детерминированное торговое правило Strategy 1: Classic Mean Reversion, основанное на кроссах Z-Score через фиксированные пороги (±2.0 для входа, 0.0 для выхода), с полностью заданной формулой Z-Score и параметрами. Все условия проверяются строго по закрытым барам без заглядывания вперёд. Стратегия применима на спот-форексе и CFD (XAUUSD, US30, BTCUSD) на таймфреймах 15M и 4H.
